title: Chiral phonons driven by chiral cavities
authors: V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, N. Shabala, R. M. Geilhufe, A. Metelmann
abstract: Lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum give rise to fundamental phenomena such as the phonon Hall effect and the Einstein-de Haas effect, offering new opportunities for manipulating angular momentum in condensed-matter systems. Generating such circularly polarized phonons requires either the use of an external magnetic field, or of polarized light pulses. The latter approach does not require the use of any magnetic response of the material, but it has limitations, in particular regarding the duration of the pulse. Consequently, any effect stemming from phonons generated by light pulses is transient. In this paper, we propose the use of a driven electromagnetic cavity as a route to generate a steady-state population of chiral phonons. We derive a general description of cavity-chiral phonon interaction, with a particular focus on modes of chiral cavities. We show that, under optimized conditions, a significant effective phonon-induced magnetic field can be generated by means of an external drive with realistic power. Our approach is specially tailored for Gamma point phonons with THz frequencies, and opens a new route for investigating chiral phonons with electromagnetic cavities.
summary: This paper proposes using a driven electromagnetic cavity as a novel platform to generate a steady-state population of chiral phonons. By modeling the cavity-phonon interaction, the authors demonstrate that this setup can induce a measurable, persistent effective magnetic field, offering a powerful tool to study phonon-mediated magnetism without relying on transient light pulses.
main_problem: The primary goal is to generate a steady-state population of chiral phonons, which carry angular momentum, to study the phono-magnetic effect, bypassing the limitations of transient excitation methods.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that using a driven electromagnetic cavity can generate a steady-state, non-zero effective phonon-induced magnetic field ($	ext{B}_{	ext{eff}}$) with realistic drive power.
method: The methodology involves deriving the general interaction Hamiltonian between the cavity electromagnetic field and the chiral phonon modes, followed by solving the driven-dissipative dynamics using the Heisenberg-Langevin equation.
model_or_system: The system is a material hosting chiral phonons coupled to a driven electromagnetic cavity. The model utilizes the cavity-phonon interaction Hamiltonian, $\hat{H}_{ac}$, and considers both chiral and linear cavity configurations.
key_observables: Effective magnetic field ($	ext{B}_{	ext{eff}}$), steady-state phonon population imbalance ($n_L - n_R$), and the phonon-cavity coupling rate ($g_k$).
important_parameters: Optimal coupling strength ($g_{opt}$), cavity decay rates ($\kappa_a, \kappa_c$), and external drive power ($P$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the small sample-cavity volume ratio ($V_s \ll V_c$) and employs the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA) for the dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the interaction between chiral phonons and the cavity field, showing the dependence of phonon population imbalance on coupling strength and detuning, and visualizing the resulting polariton frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for steady-state generation to deriving the general interaction Hamiltonian, applying this to chiral and linear cavity setups, solving the resulting driven-dissipative dynamics, and finally calculating the resulting effective magnetic field.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems because it models the coherent, driven coupling between two distinct quantum subsystems (photons/cavity modes and phonons) to engineer a macroscopic quantum response (magnetization) in a steady state.

Spintronics.note: The paper's core mechanism—generating a measurable, steady-state effective magnetic field ($\mathbf{B}_{eff}$) using cavity-phonon coupling—directly relates to the study of magnon/spin-photon polaritons and non-equilibrium phases in hybrid spin-photon systems.
